jobs.title: Contract GTM Recruiter
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

At Cursor, Recruiting is one of the most important functions in the company. We believe every hire changes the trajectory of the business, and recruiters are expected to operate as strategic partners to leaders.

As a GTM Recruiter, you will be responsible for building and scaling the teams that drive Cursor's growth, including Sales, Field Engineering, Customer Success, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, and GTM Leadership. You will partner directly with leaders to define talent strategy, shape org design, calibrate hiring bars, and attract exceptional talent.

This is a highly visible role with significant ownership and influence. You will be expected to think like a business leader, challenge assumptions, bring market intelligence to the table, and help us make some of the most important decisions in the company: who we hire and how we scale.

The best recruiters at Cursor are talent magnets, trusted advisors, exceptional operators, and relentless talent evaluators who care deeply about quality, speed, and candidate experience.

What you’ll do

  • Partner directly with GTM leaders to understand business goals, hiring priorities, and organizational needs.

  • Act as a strategic talent advisor, helping leaders define roles, build teams, and make informed hiring decisions.

  • Own the end-to-end recruiting process from kickoff through close, driving urgency and excellence at every stage.

  • Build and execute talent strategies for critical and high-impact searches across the GTM organization.

  • Identify, engage, and close exceptional talent through proactive outreach, referrals, networking, and relationship building.

  • Maintain an exceptionally high hiring bar and serve as a trusted voice in talent assessment and calibration discussions.

  • Bring market insights, competitive intelligence, and talent trends to leaders to inform hiring strategy and workforce planning.

  • Drive an outstanding candidate experience while ensuring every interaction reflects Cursor's values and culture.

  • Partner with hiring managers to continuously improve interview design, hiring rigor, and selection processes.

  • Influence offer strategy, negotiation, and close plans for top candidates.

  • Leverage data and recruiting metrics to identify bottlenecks, improve efficiency, and drive better hiring outcomes.

  • Help build scalable recruiting programs, processes, and best practices as we continue to grow.

You may be a fit if

  • 5+ years of recruiting experience, ideally within high-growth technology companies.

  • Experience hiring GTM talent across Sales, Field Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, or GTM Leadership.

  • Proven ability to operate as a strategic partner to executives and hiring managers.

  • Strong sourcing and talent mapping skills with a track record of identifying and engaging top-tier talent.

  • Exceptional assessment skills and strong judgment around talent, hiring, and team building.

  • Excellent communication and influence skills, with the ability to challenge, advise, and build trust with senior stakeholders.

  • Strong operational rigor and ability to manage multiple high-priority searches simultaneously.

  • Data-driven mindset with the ability to use insights and metrics to improve outcomes.

  • Demonstrated success closing highly competitive candidates.

  • High agency, strong ownership mentality, and a bias toward action.

  • Excitement about AI, developer tools, and helping build one of the most important companies in software.

jobs.title: Solutions Architect - Japan
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We’re hiring Solution Architects to help the world’s best engineering organizations figure out what AI-native software development actually looks like in production.

This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside Cursor’s most strategic enterprise accounts. You’ll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI.

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. You’ll help customers move from initial excitement to deeply integrating engineering workflows that teams rely on every day. That means understanding how modern software organizations operate, identifying where Cursor can create the most leverage, and helping customers scale adoption across teams, platforms, and workflows over time.

This role is highly hands-on. You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

 

What you'll do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development

  • Roll out Cursor across strategic engineering organizations

  • Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

  • Help developers integrate Cursor into real production workflows, not isolated demos

  • Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

  • Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

Expand Cursor Across the Organization

  • Identify where Cursor should expand next inside the customer environment

  • Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

  • Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

  • Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

  • Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

  • Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

  • Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

  • Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

  • Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

  • Connect Cursor usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

  • Help customers communicate the value of Cursor internally and build momentum for broader adoption

  • Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

Help Make Cursor Indispensable

  • Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

  • Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Cursor over time

  • Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

  • Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without

Shape the Future of the Product

  • Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

  • Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

  • Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

  • Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

     

You may be a fit if

  • You have a strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

  • You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

  • You are willing to travel to customers needed

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. You’ll help customers move from initial excitement to deeply integrating engineering workflows that teams rely on every day. That means understanding how modern software organizations operate, identifying where Cursor can create the most leverage, and helping customers scale adoption across teams, platforms, and workflows over time.

This role is highly hands-on. You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO


HELP ENGINEERING TEAMS ADOPT AI-NATIVE DEVELOPMENT

 - Roll out Cursor across strategic engineering organizations

 - Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

 - Help developers integrate Cursor into real production workflows, not isolated demos

 - Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

 - Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly


EXPAND CURSOR ACROSS THE ORGANIZATION

 - Identify where Cursor should expand next inside the customer environment

 - Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

 - Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

 - Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

 - Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments


BECOME A TRUSTED TECHNICAL PARTNER

 - Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

 - Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

 - Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

 - Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

 - Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves


DRIVE REAL CUSTOMER OUTCOMES

 - Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

 - Connect Cursor usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

 - Help customers communicate the value of Cursor internally and build momentum for broader adoption

 - Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization


HELP MAKE CURSOR INDISPENSABLE

 - Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

 - Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Cursor over time

 - Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

 - Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without


SHAPE THE FUTURE OF THE PRODUCT

 - Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

 - Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

 - Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

 - Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns
   
    


YOU MAY BE A FIT IF

 - You have a strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

 - You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

 - You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

 - You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

 - You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

 - You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

 - You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

 - You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

 - You are willing to travel to customers needed

jobs.title: Field Engineer, Life Sciences
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

We're hiring Field Engineers to partner with prospective and strategic enterprise customers across Life Sciences. You'll be the technical face of Cursor for the scientific organizations shortening the path from lab to market: helping programmers, researchers, scientists, and commercial teams evaluate Cursor, running proofs of concept, and making sure they see the full value of agentic coding in their real workflows.

You'll work hand-in-hand with Sales, Product, and Engineering as a deal partner, not a demo resource. You'll scope solutions, demonstrate capabilities, and act as a trusted advisor across the stakeholders that matter in Life Sciences: engineering leaders, architects, developers, scientific computing, R&D, and commercial IT. This is a highly customer-facing role where deep technical fluency, commercial instinct, and clear communication drive adoption and influence product direction.

What you'll do

  • Partner with AEs to own technical discovery, demos, POCs, and expansion with technical validation

  • Build trusted relationships across engineering, scientific computing, R&D, and commercial IT

  • Go deep in research-heavy and regulated environments: developer workflows, AI tooling, complex setups

  • Help customers connect Cursor to outcomes that matter: faster R&D cycles and a shorter path from lab to market

  • Deliver technical presentations, whiteboards, and workshops for scientific and commercial audiences

  • Act as the customer's technical advocate internally with Product and Engineering

  • Partner with post-sales to hand off cleanly and set up onboarding for success

  • Stay sharp on Cursor and the competitive landscape so you can go toe to toe in the room

You may be a fit if

  • You have strong communication skills and executive presence, equally comfortable coding alongside developers or presenting to CTOs and scientific leaders

  • You understand the SDLC and can connect technical detail to business and scientific impact

  • You have hands-on technical fluency (not full-time eng): workflows, AI tooling, complex environments

  • You have deal-partner instinct: co-own with AEs and navigate complex stakeholder maps

  • You're customer-obsessed and can translate technical detail into why it matters for the organization

  • You have experience in Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Pre-Sales, or Consulting

  • You're excited by Life Sciences and comfortable learning regulated / research-heavy orgs fast

  • You're motivated by putting AI in the hands of people accelerating benefits for humanity

jobs.title: Data Analyst, User Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

The User Operations team owns the support experience for Cursor's users - from individual developers to our largest enterprise accounts. As we've scaled across regions, the volume and richness of our support data has grown faster than our ability to make sense of it. We're looking for a Data Analyst to change that.

This role sits inside our Product and Engineering organization with a dotted line to the Head of User Operations and owns the data and reporting layer for Support. You'll turn ticket data, SLA performance, customer sentiment, and product signal into the dashboards and analysis that leadership uses to run the org - and into the evidence Product and Engineering use to decide what to fix next. Support is one of the clearest signals we have about where the product is working and where it isn't. Your job is to make that signal legible.

 

What you'll do

  • Build and own the reporting layer for Support: ticket volume, SLA attainment, resolution times, help center performance, CSAT/CES/sentiment, and capacity utilization across regions and tiers

  • Partner with Support leadership to turn open questions - "are we getting faster but less accurate?", "where is enterprise pain actually concentrated?" - into analysis that drives decisions

  • Maintain the multi-signal model behind bug and issue prioritization, weighting frequency, breadth, support cost, and sentiment, so Engineering sees a defensible picture of what impacts users most

  • Design dashboards for two audiences: internal operational views for managers, and customer-facing views for enterprise accounts

  • Own data quality, governance, and reliability across Support data products, including our ticketing data and internal commitments

  • Surface Voice of Customer trends to Product, Engineering, and GTM, and help close the loop between what users report and what actually gets built

 

You may be a fit if

  • You have 5+ years of experience in data analytics, analytics engineering, or a similar role

  • You have strong SQL skills - this is your primary toolkit - and you're comfortable building models and transformations (dbt or equivalent)

  • You've built reporting and dashboards in production that people actually depend on, not one-off charts

  • You can take a vague operational question and turn it into the right analysis without a playbook

  • You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and you're honest about what the data does and doesn't support

  • You're self-directed and comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end

jobs.title: Regional Director, Forward Deployed Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We're building a Forward Deployed Engineering team to close the gap between the value our enterprise customers expect from Cursor and the value they're actually getting. FDEs don't advise, they embed directly with customer engineering teams, build production-grade Cursor workflows, and transfer the habits and culture that compound long after the engagement ends. The measure of success is what's different at day 30, not what got shipped.

We're looking for a Regional Director, Forward Deployed Engineering to lead and help scale this team. You'll manage a growing team of FDEs working across our most strategic enterprise accounts, own what makes a world-class FDE engagement, and stay close enough to the work to escalate, coach, and course-correct in real time. You will serve as the primary point of contact for customers, owning both project delivery and the day-to-day relationship, while also identifying and scoping new opportunities. You'll also build our partner FDE track — training and enabling GSI and consulting partners who extend this motion at scale.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who combines deep technical credibility, strong people management, and the judgment to keep engagements scoped tight, delivered fast, and worth repeating.

What you’ll do

  • Sell

    • Own the full arc from technical discovery to executive close — partnering with Sales and Account teams to qualify opportunities, leading architecture reviews, surfacing integration complexity and infrastructure constraints, and scoping engagements with enough precision to de-risk delivery before a line of code is written

    • Build and present proposals that translate ambiguous customer problems into concrete, time-boxed deliverables with clear ROI

    • Sell the vision and the plan to C-suite stakeholders who need to believe in both the outcome and the team delivering it

    • Drive deal strategy on strategic accounts; your technical credibility is a direct lever on close rates for six- and seven-figure engagements

    Deliver

    • Serve as executive technical sponsor on your region's highest-priority engagements and manage stakeholder relationships from IC engineers to C-suite

    • Ensure delivery quality across your team's projects: appropriate scoping, milestone tracking, technical standards, and clean handoffs to customer engineering teamsTranslate between business outcomes and technical implementation in both directions

    • Identify and escalate product gaps, integration friction, and recurring customer pain back to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to drive roadmap decisions

    • Manage active engagements: escalate on complex builds, coach FDEs on scoping and delivery decisions, and step in directly on accounts where the stakes are highest

    • Build reusable playbooks that make the broader FDE org more capable over time

    Manage People

    • Lead, develop, and scale a team of 6–8 Forward Deployed Engineers working strategic FDE projects

    • Hire top-tier FDE talent; set clear expectations, technical performance standards, and career growth paths for a team where "excellent" means actually shipping in production

    • Coach FDEs through the hardest problems in the field — scoping under deal pressure, building alongside senior technical stakeholders, and knowing when to protect scope vs. when to flex

    • Build and scale the partner FDE track — train, enable, and hold the quality bar for GSI and consulting partners who carry the FDE motion forward at volume

You may be a fit if

  • You have 8+ years of experience leading technical teams that build and ship in production — Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering, or a similar function where writing and reviewing code is part of the job

  • You have experience with software development and coding in Python, Javascript/Typescript

  • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows in production, not just prototypes, and have debugged real-world model failures

  • You can diagnose a complex enterprise engineering environment quickly, identify the highest-leverage intervention, and scope a meaningful engagement

  • You've built and scaled IC-level technical teams and know what excellence looks like in the field: sharp scoping, clean delivery, and knowledge that stays at the customer long after the engagement closes

jobs.title: Sales Development Leader, APJ
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

Sales Development Leader, APJ

Location: Sydney, Australia (In Office)

About the Role

We are hiring a Sales Development Leader, APJ to build and lead Cursor’s Sales Development organization across Asia Pacific. Based in our Sydney office, this is a frontline leadership role responsible for hiring, coaching, and developing a high-performing team of Account Associates that generate pipeline and accelerate customer adoption across the region.

This isn’t a traditional SDR organization focused solely on cold outreach. Our Sales Development team partners closely with Growth, Marketing, RevOps, and Sales to identify buying signals, engage customers at the right moment, and create highly personalized outreach informed by product usage, PLG signals, and creative automation. You’ll help your team balance modern, signal-based engagement with disciplined outbound prospecting to consistently create new opportunities across commercial and enterprise accounts.

You’ll be responsible for building a strong team culture, driving execution against pipeline goals, coaching early-career talent, and continuously improving how Cursor engages prospective customers across APJ. This role is ideal for a hands-on sales leader who enjoys coaching people, experimenting with new approaches, and building scalable operating rhythms in a fast-growing company.

This is a full-time, in-office leadership role based in our Sydney office.

What You’ll Do

  • Hire, onboard, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Account Associates supporting the APJ business.

  • Lead the team’s day-to-day execution against pipeline generation goals, activity metrics, and conversion targets.

  • Partner with Growth, RevOps, Marketing, and Sales to execute signal-based outbound programs leveraging product usage, PLG insights, events, and other buying signals.

  • Help define and refine regional sales development playbooks that combine modern automation with highly personalized customer engagement.

  • Coach Account Associates on prospecting, discovery, qualification, messaging, and customer engagement to consistently improve pipeline quality.

  • Establish a strong operating cadence through regular pipeline reviews, one-on-ones, performance coaching, team meetings, and career development.

  • Monitor team performance, identify trends, and use data to continuously improve productivity, conversion rates, and execution.

  • Collaborate closely with Commercial and Enterprise Sales leaders to ensure high-quality pipeline generation and seamless opportunity handoffs.

  • Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, accountability, and continuous learning.

  • Develop future sales talent by creating clear career pathways into Account Executive and other GTM roles across Cursor.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of SaaS sales experience, including experience leading frontline Sales Development or SDR teams.

  • Proven success hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing SDRs or Account Associates in a fast-paced technology company.

  • Experience building predictable outbound pipeline generation through a combination of prospecting, automation, and data-driven experimentation.

  • Strong operational discipline with experience managing team performance through metrics, coaching, and structured operating cadences.

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Marketing, Growth, RevOps, and Sales to improve pipeline generation and conversion.

  • Passion for coaching and developing early-career sales talent into successful GTM professionals.

  • Curiosity about AI, developer tools, or technical products, with the ability to help teams engage technical buyers effectively.

  • Comfortable operating in a high-growth, fast-changing environment where experimentation and continuous improvement are expected.

  • Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills with a collaborative, builder’s mindset.

  • Experience with AI products, growth automation platforms, PLG motions, or developer-focused technology is a plus.

jobs.title: GTM, Emerging Products
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

The Incubation Team is a new team within Cursor responsible for bringing Cursor's next products to market. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Sales to validate customer demand, refine positioning, and build repeatable go-to-market motions before products scale to the broader organization.

Each new product gets a dedicated team. There's no established pipeline or playbook. You'll work directly with customers to understand what they need, what they'll pay for, and what it takes to turn an emerging product into a successful business.

This is not a traditional sales role. You'll spend as much time learning as you do selling - leading customer discovery, shaping product direction, and influencing go-to-market strategy.

If you're excited by ambiguity, enjoy being close to the product, and want to help build what's next, you'll fit right in.

What you’ll do

  • Product expertise and solution leadership: Serve as the GTM expert for incubation products, developing deep knowledge of customer pain points, target personas, product capabilities, competitive alternatives, and positioning.

  • Account strategy and opportunity creation: Identify opportunities within existing customers and develop a clear point of view on where emerging products can create value. Partner with Core AEs and ADMs on account strategy while independently driving incubation motions

  • Customer discovery and validation: Lead deep discovery to understand adoption drivers, barriers, product gaps, and buying motivations. Use customer interactions, evaluations, wins, and losses to shape product requirements, positioning, and go-to-market strategy.

  • Technical and executive selling: Build champions, navigate engineering leaders and executive stakeholders, and lead value-based sales motions that convert opportunities into product adoption

  • Complex opportunity ownership: Own incubation opportunities end-to-end, coordinating across account teams, Product, Engineering, Field Engineering, and customer stakeholders

  • Business building: Help determine not only whether customers will adopt a new offering, but why they would do so and what it takes to build a repeatable business around it

You may be a fit if

  • You're genuinely entrepreneurial and curious, and energized by building something new

  • You see the 0→1 opportunity as the primary draw. You're excited by the challenge of figuring out what customers want, what they'll buy, and how a new product becomes a real business.

  • You want to be close to the product, understand why it wins and loses, and help shape what comes next

  • You’re comfortable operating without a playbook and making progress through ambiguity

  • You move fast, and adapt as products, customer feedback, and priorities evolve

  • You’ve sold at an early-stage company, and know how to sell transformational outcomes, not just product features or manage inbound demand

jobs.title: Integrated Campaigns, APJ
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor is hiring a Senior Campaigns Manager to join our integrated campaigns team and help shape how Cursor shows up to enterprise audiences.

You will own high-priority campaigns that turn broad company priorities into focused, executable programs, working seamlessly across product marketing, sales, customer marketing, field, and leadership. The campaign strategies and programs you develop will shape our narrative in the market, create demand, generate & accelerate pipeline, and support customer growth.

This is a high-agency role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally comfortable identifying the right audience, building the campaign brief, shaping the message, coordinating cross-functional partners, launching programs across channels, and measuring what is actually working. Equal parts creative and analytical, you will think outside the box to propose original ideas and inventive audience engagement strategies, while bringing a data-driven mindset and the operational rigor required for high-impact execution.

 

What you’ll do

  • Concept, develop, and run integrated campaigns end to end.

    • Lead the strategy and audience selection through launch, optimization, and reporting.

    • Design the end-to-end campaign architecture, including the full-funnel content engine, channel strategies, promotional offers, program mix, and hand-offs from marketing to sales.

    • Translate company priorities into focused campaign plans with clear goals, messaging, milestones, owners, and success metrics.

    • Identify the highest-leverage assets needed to support campaign performance, including messaging frameworks, email nurtures, landing page copy, field activation ideas, customer story packaging, and sales-facing materials.

    • Bring multi-channel expertise to deliver campaigns via digital, web, email, online events, direct mail, social, events, sales plays, and more, all in partnership with functional and regional teams.

  • Strengthen cross-functional alignment, unifying all parts of the business around top go-to-market priorities.

    • Develop trusted relationships and facilitate integrated collaboration across product marketing, field marketing, performance marketing, growth marketing, strategic events, and design.

    • Work with creative partners to brief campaigns clearly and carry the message through across formats, channels, and moments in market.

    • Align closely with sales stakeholders to identify top priorities, build programs for strategic accounts, and ensure campaign initiatives are closely tied to revenue impact.

  • Establish measurement frameworks, KPIs, and scaleable processes.

    • Own campaign performance by measuring, analyzing, and reporting on the impact of campaign on pipeline, revenue, target account penetration, and the demand funnel. Share learnings regularly to improve overall campaign efficacy.

    • Work closely with operations and analytics partners to define the right KPIs, shape useful dashboards and reporting, and surface actionable account or campaign insights to the business.

    • Help establish repeatable campaign systems, workflows, and handoffs that let the function scale without becoming fragmented

  • Adapt campaigns for Cursor’s most strategic accounts and business priorities.

    • Build campaigns for enterprise and strategic audiences, including vertical, segment, buying-group, or use-case-specific motions. Translate vertical-specific messaging and proof points into campaign activations that make Cursor feel relevant to the priorities of different enterprise audiences.

    • Build 1:few ABM motions & ABM-at-scale programs for priority accounts or segments, in partnership with sales and field teams.

 

You may be a fit if

  • You’ve built integrated B2B campaigns across multiple channels and know how to connect content, email, digital, field, and sales motions into cohesive, high-impact motions.

  • You know how to turn a campaign idea into a real operating plan — from narrative and audience strategy through asset development, launch, field enablement, lead follow-up, and reporting.

  • You can take complex, ambiguous problems and bring structure, clarity, and a clear recommendation.

  • You’re comfortable being both strategic and hands-on — you can set direction, write a brief, shape the content, and help get the work shipped.

  • You have strong instincts for what makes a campaign cohesive across content, creative, distribution, and follow-up.

  • You’re comfortable working across both global strategy and regional execution, and can adapt campaigns thoughtfully for different markets without losing the core narrative.

  • You have strong instincts for what makes enterprise campaigns resonate with senior technical and business buyers.

  • You thrive in creative, fast-paced environments where original thinking and bias to action are celebrated.

  • You can shift between air cover demand generation and more targeted programs for strategic accounts, named accounts, and priority verticals.

  • You balance thoughtful dedication to quality with a clear focus on impact and ability to execute with sharp, decisive speed.

 

Experience that helps

  • You have 10+ years of experience owning integrated campaign strategy and execution for a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.

  • You have extensive familiarity with lead-routing & handoff. You’re able to diagnose funnel health and quickly course correct in tight alignment with your SDR counterparts.

  • You have a proven track record of building campaigns for enterprise audiences, including technical decision-makers, executives, and complex buying groups.

  • You have owned pipeline goals in the past, and have experience using pipeline, engagement, and revenue signals to optimize campaign performance. You iterate continuously, quickly adapting to new signals, business priorities, and shifts in the market.

  • You have experience running ABM / strategic-account programs that support multithreading, expansion, or deal acceleration.

  • You bring a sharp understanding of the AI market and technical buyer personas (CTOs, CIOs, Senior Engineering leaders) to develop campaign activation plans.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Storage
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the Storage team at Cursor, you'll own the data layer that underpins every product surface: the databases, caches, and the strategy for how teams provision, query, and scale their data stores.

Millions of developers depend on Cursor every day, and the future of our storage architecture is one of the highest-leverage problems at the company: get it right, and every team ships faster, every product surface gets more reliable, and Cursor can scale to meet explosive demand. You'll design and execute the path to a robust, multi-database topology built for that growth.

Example projects include...

  • Designing the next-generation data architecture: evolving our storage layer into a partitioned, resilient topology that keeps pace with Cursor's rapid growth.

  • Building query attribution and guardrails: instrumenting every database query by service, catching bad patterns before they hit production, and making it impossible to ship problematic queries without review.

  • Defining the "when to use what" strategy for data stores: creating clear guidance and golden pathways so every team picks the right engine for their workload without second-guessing.

  • Owning cache infrastructure end-to-end: reliability, capacity planning, and patterns that let product teams move fast without worrying about cache correctness.

You may be a fit if

  • You have deep experience with relational databases at scale, especially Postgres, MySQL, or similar OLTP systems.

  • You've tackled database sharding, migration, or decomposition problems in production environments.

  • You understand the tradeoffs between different storage engines and can help teams make the right choices for their workloads.

  • You care about operational excellence: backups, monitoring, query performance, and capacity planning are things you think about proactively.

  • You have strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building systems that other engineers depend on.

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

#LI-DNI

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer, Services Platform at Cursor, you'll build the platform-level primitives that make it hard for product teams to build brittle systems and easy to build resilient ones.

Cursor is scaling fast, hundreds of engineers shipping to millions of developers, and your core focus will be the abstractions that make that sustainable: service provisioning, deploy tooling, workflow orchestration, and defining what it means to own and operate a service at Cursor. You'll work at the intersection of developer experience and production reliability, building the golden pathways that every engineering team runs on.

Example projects include...

  • Establishing durable workflow orchestration as a first-class platform: defining best practices, building shared abstractions, and creating the standard that every team uses for reliable, long-running workflows.

  • Designing a declarative service configuration framework that makes it trivial to provision, deploy, and operate new services, so spinning up a new backend goes from days to minutes.

  • Defining the contract for service ownership: what it means to own a service, how services integrate with Cursor's infrastructure abstractions, and building the service catalogue so incidents get resolved in minutes, not hours.

You may be a fit if

  • You have experience building internal developer platforms, service frameworks, or infrastructure abstractions that other engineers depend on.

  • You've worked extensively with Temporal, durable workflow engines, or similar orchestration systems and have strong opinions on best practices.

  • You care deeply about developer experience. You think about how other engineers interact with your systems and design for simplicity and correctness by default.

  • You have experience with deployment tooling, CI/CD pipelines, or service mesh architectures.

  • You understand the tradeoffs in microservice vs. monolith architectures and can help teams navigate service decomposition pragmatically.

  • You have strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy shipping production systems that make the entire organization more productive.

Applying

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach out to schedule 2-3 short technicals. After, we'll schedule an onsite in our office, where you'll work on a small project, discuss ideas, and meet the team.

jobs.title: Solutions Architect, Central Europe
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

We’re hiring Solution Architects to help the world’s best engineering organizations figure out what AI-native software development actually looks like in production.

This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside Cursor’s most strategic enterprise accounts. You’ll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI.

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. You’ll help customers move from initial excitement to deeply integrating engineering workflows that teams rely on every day. That means understanding how modern software organizations operate, identifying where Cursor can create the most leverage, and helping customers scale adoption across teams, platforms, and workflows over time.

This role is highly hands-on. You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

 

What You’ll Do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development

  • Roll out Cursor across strategic engineering organizations

  • Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

  • Help developers integrate Cursor into real production workflows, not isolated demos

  • Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

  • Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

Expand Cursor Across the Organization

  • Identify where Cursor should expand next inside the customer environment

  • Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

  • Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

  • Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

  • Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

  • Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

  • Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

  • Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

  • Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

  • Connect Cursor usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

  • Help customers communicate the value of Cursor internally and build momentum for broader adoption

  • Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

Help Make Cursor Indispensable

  • Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

  • Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Cursor over time

  • Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

  • Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without

Shape the Future of the Product

  • Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

  • Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

  • Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

  • Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

 

You’ll might be a fit if

  • You have strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

  • You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

We're hiring a Regional Director, Field Engineering to build and lead a high impact pre-sales Field Engineering team focused on Cursor's healthcare vertical — supporting our fastest growing enterprise accounts across health systems, payers, and healthcare software companies. This role sits at the intersection of Sales, Product, and Engineering and is responsible for ensuring our technical pre-sales motion scales with quality, speed, and credibility.

As the Regional Director, Field Engineering, you’ll manage and develop Field Engineers who partner closely with AEs to run technical discovery, demos, and proofs of concept tailored to Healthcare buyers. You’ll also stay close to customers and deals yourself, coaching in real time, unblocking complex evaluations, and ensuring Cursor is positioned as the best AI-native development platform for healthcare engineering organizations.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who combines technical fluency, strong people management, and excellent cross-functional judgment.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, coach, and scale a team of Field Engineers supporting enterprise opportunities

  • Partner closely with Sales leadership and AEs to drive high quality technical discovery, demos, and POCs

  • Establish best practices for evaluations, proof-of-concept execution, and technical deal strategy, accounting for healthcare-specific requirements (HIPAA, data governance, legacy systems integration)

  • Serve as an escalation point for complex customer evaluations and high-stakes enterprise deals in the healthcare space

  • Hire, onboard, and develop top-tier Field Engineering talent with healthcare or regulated-industry domain experience; set clear expectations and career paths

  • Act as the voice of the field internally, feeding customer and prospect insights back to Product and Engineering

  • Ensure tight handoffs with post-sales teams to support successful customer onboarding and adoption

  • Maintain deep knowledge of Cursor’s product, roadmap, and competitive landscape

You may be a fit if

  • You have 4+ years experience leading Field Engineers, Solutions Architects, or Pre-Sales teams in enterprise software, with meaningful exposure to healthcare, health tech, or another regulated industry

  • You have direct experience navigating healthcare buyer environments — health systems, payers, or healthcare software vendors — including compliance, security, and procurement dynamics specific to the space

  • You have proven your ability to partner effectively with Sales while maintaining technical integrity and customer trust

  • You are comfortable operating in customer-facing, high-pressure deal environments and guiding teams through complexity

  • You have strong communication skills and executive presence, and can engage developers, architects, CTOs, and healthcare IT leadership

  • You have a builder mindset: you thrive in fast-moving, startup environments and enjoy creating structure where little exists

Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We're hiring a Regional Director, Public Sector Field Engineering to build and lead Cursor's technical pre-sales organization supporting Federal, State, Local, and Education (SLED) accounts. This is a founding leadership role for the vertical — you'll be responsible for standing up the Field Engineering team, technical pre-sales motion, and evaluation playbook that brings Cursor's AI-native development platform into government agencies, public institutions, and the contractors that serve them.

As RD, Public Sector Field Engineering, you'll manage and develop Field Engineers who partner closely with Public Sector AEs to run technical discovery, demos, and proofs of concept inside government procurement and security constraints. You'll also stay close to customers and deals yourself, coaching in real time, unblocking complex evaluations, and ensuring Cursor is positioned as the best AI-native development platform for public sector engineering organizations.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who combines technical fluency, public sector domain credibility, strong people management, and excellent cross-functional judgment.

What you'll do

  • Build and lead a Field Engineering team supporting Federal and SLED enterprise opportunities

  • Partner closely with Public Sector Sales leadership and AEs to drive high quality technical discovery, demos, and POCs within government evaluation processes

  • Establish best practices for evaluations, proof-of-concept execution, and technical deal strategy that account for public sector requirements — FedRAMP, StateRAMP, air-gapped/on-prem environments, security authorization processes

  • Serve as an escalation point for complex customer evaluations and high-stakes public sector deals

  • Hire, onboard, and develop top-tier Field Engineering talent with public sector or regulated-environment domain experience; set clear expectations and career paths

  • Act as the voice of the field internally, feeding agency and institutional customer insights back to Product and Engineering to shape the public sector roadmap

  • Partner with Legal, Security, and Compliance to ensure technical evaluations meet the bar required to sell into government environments

  • Ensure tight handoffs with post-sales teams to support successful onboarding and adoption in public sector accounts

  • Maintain deep knowledge of Cursor's product, roadmap, and competitive landscape, plus the public sector security and compliance landscape

You may be a fit if

  • You have 6+ years experience leading Field Engineers, Solutions Architects, or Pre-Sales teams in enterprise software, with meaningful time spent in Federal and/or SLED environments

  • You have direct experience navigating public sector technical evaluation processes — security authorizations, compliance reviews, and procurement-driven POC requirements

  • You have a strong technical foundation and fluency in modern software development workflows, AI tooling, and developer productivity

  • You have proven your ability to partner effectively with Sales while maintaining technical integrity and customer trust in high-stakes, high-scrutiny deal environments

  • You are comfortable operating in customer-facing, high-pressure deal environments and guiding teams through complexity

  • You have strong communication skills and executive presence, able to engage agency technical leadership, CTOs, and compliance stakeholders

  • You have a builder mindset: you thrive in fast-moving, startup environments and enjoy creating structure where little exists

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Field
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

We're looking for our first Technical Program Manager to work with our largest enterprise customers and help them adopt Cursor. This is a highly customer-facing role. You'll partner closely with customer engineering teams and internal stakeholders to drive complex deployments across engineering, security, IT, and executive stakeholders. You'll be responsible for ensuring customers achieve measurable outcomes while helping Cursor scale its enterprise motion.

As our first TPM, you'll also help define how we work. You'll build the playbooks, processes, and operating rhythms that allow us to support increasingly large and complex customer deployments.

What You'll Do

  • Own the success of our most strategic customer deployments, from initial planning through organization-wide rollout.

  • Act as the quarterback across customer stakeholders and Cursor teams, driving alignment, execution, and decision-making.

  • Turn ambiguity into clear plans, identify risks before they become problems, and keep complex programs moving forward.

  • Build trusted relationships with engineering leaders, executives, and technical teams at some of the world's most sophisticated companies.

  • Create the playbooks, processes, and operating model for how Cursor scales enterprise deployments.

  • Bring customer feedback directly into Product and Engineering, helping shape the future of Cursor.


You might be a fit if

  • Experience leading large, cross-functional technical projects with significant stakeholder complexity.

  • Strong customer-facing skills and a track record of building trust with senior technical and business leaders.

  • Ability to understand technical systems and communicate effectively with engineers.

  • Exceptional organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for direction.

  • Bias toward action and a willingness to dive in wherever needed to help customers succeed.

  • Experience with enterprise software deployments, technical consulting, solutions architecture, or program management.

  • Background working with developer tools, infrastructure, AI products, or technical platforms.

  • Experience partnering with large engineering organizations and executive stakeholders.

  • Previous experience at a high-growth startup.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Agent & Product Security
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor’s agents work inside the codebases of some of the most security-conscious engineering organizations in the world — holding credentials, reading untrusted content, running tools, and shipping changes. Today they act on authority delegated per task. Where we’re headed, they’ll work more like coworkers: autonomous over long horizons, holding standing responsibilities, initiating work, and collaborating with people and other agents. The security models that future needs — identity and accountability for autonomous workers, standing authority rather than per-task permission, agent-to-agent trust, oversight that scales with always-on autonomy — mostly don’t exist yet.

As Engineering Manager for Agent & Product Security, you’ll lead the team that makes agentic software development trustworthy. This team owns the security boundaries between customers, data, tools, repositories, workspaces, and agent authority across Cursor’s product and agents and designs the primitives behind them: agent identity, delegated authority, policy enforcement, secure tool execution, and prompt-injection containment. Little of this has settled precedent, so the team’s decisions carry unusual weight for Cursor and for how the industry approaches these problems.

Security here is tightly coupled to product strategy: customers adopt agent autonomy as fast as we can make it trustworthy, so the boundaries your team makes safe directly determine what the product can ship. You’ll help set that direction.

What you’ll do

  • Chart the path from supervised agents to trusted autonomous ones: define the security primitives that enable agent autonomy, and lead the team that builds them.

  • Engineer the isolation that makes Cursor safe to run inside customers’ most valuable codebases: tenancy, workspace, secret, and data protections designed for real adversaries.

  • Build the authority infrastructure autonomous agents need: identity, scoped permissions, policy enforcement, and secure tool execution, so an agent can hold real responsibility with verifiable limits and full accountability.

  • Build customer-facing security controls that are understandable, usable, and strong enough for Cursor’s most security-sensitive customers, with crisp success metrics for security outcomes.

  • Hire, coach, and grow a high-performing security engineering team while staying technically close to the work: write and review code where useful, and keep execution fast and technically grounded.

You may be a fit if

  • You’ve led engineering teams shipping production systems with high security, reliability, or platform stakes — and you want a problem space where much of the answer isn’t written down yet.

  • You have strong product and systems judgment: you can reason from user workflows to architecture, threat models, enforcement points, and operational tradeoffs — and you see security as something that enables product capability, not only restricts it.

  • You understand modern application security, authorization, tenancy, identity, secrets, data isolation, and secure-by-default platform design.

  • You have good instincts about AI agents: how they use tools, where authority should come from, how prompt injection and exfiltration show up in practice, and how to build mitigations that hold up against creative adversaries.

  • You’re comfortable operating in ambiguity: you can set strategy where precedent is thin, commit to a direction, and stay close enough to the implementation to know when to change it.

  • You can partner well across product, infrastructure, ML, and customer-facing teams.

#LI-DNI

jobs.title: Strategic Enterprise Account Executive - India
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

As a Strategic Account Executive for India, you’ll be one of the foundational members of Cursor’s enterprise sales team in the region. You’ll help large engineering organizations discover, adopt, and expand their use of Cursor, owning strategic accounts across APJ and working directly with engineering leaders, CTOs, developer platform teams, and procurement stakeholders.

This is a rare opportunity to bring a product engineers already love into some of India's most sophisticated technology, financial services, enterprise, and digital-native organizations and to help shape how software gets built in the AI era.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own a named book of strategic enterprise accounts across India, driving new logo acquisition and expansion revenue

  • Run a disciplined, full-cycle sales process from prospecting and discovery through evaluation, negotiation, and close

  • Build and execute account strategies that connect Cursor’s capabilities to the technical and business priorities of engineering leaders, CTOs, and developer platform teams

  • Create pipeline through outbound prospecting, executive mapping, inbound follow-up, partner referrals, and your own network

  • Partner closely with Sales Engineering, Product, and Customer Success to deliver high-quality evaluations and ensure customers realize value quickly

  • Navigate complex enterprise buying processes, including security reviews, legal negotiations, procurement, and multi-stakeholder approval cycles

  • Serve as the voice of India's enterprise customers internally, sharing market feedback and deal learnings with Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and GTM leadership

  • Help establish Cursor’s enterprise presence in India by building repeatable motions, local market insights, and early customer references

  • Consistently meet and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets

 

You may be a fit if

  • You have 5+ years of enterprise B2B sales experience, ideally selling developer tools, infrastructure, cloud, security, AI, or other technical SaaS products to engineering-led organizations

  • You have experience selling into strategic or large enterprise accounts in India

  • You’re comfortable navigating complex buying committees across engineering, IT, security, legal, procurement, finance, and executive stakeholders

  • You’re a true hunter: you proactively build pipeline from scratch through outbound prospecting, creative sourcing, executive engagement, and persistent follow-up

  • You have strong command of pipeline management, account planning, and forecasting across a strategic book of business

  • You’re energized by technical products and can hold credible conversations with senior engineers, platform leaders, and CTOs about how Cursor fits into modern development workflows

  • You’re a self-starter who thrives in an early-stage, resource-constrained environment and can build process, playbooks, and regional learnings as you go

  • You care deeply about AI and believe transforming how software is written is one of the most important problems to work on right now

jobs.title: Field Engineer - India
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

We’re hiring Field Engineers to partner with prospective and strategic enterprise customers. As a Field Engineer, you’ll be the technical face of Anysphere in the field, helping customers evaluate Cursor, guiding them through proofs of concept, and ensuring they see the full value of AI in their engineering workflows.

You’ll work hand-in-hand with Sales, Product, and Engineering to scope solutions, demonstrate capabilities, and act as a trusted advisor to technical stakeholders. This is a highly customer-facing role where you’ll combine deep technical fluency with strong communication skills to drive adoption and influence product direction.

What you’ll do

  • Partner with Account Executives to lead technical discovery, demos, and proof-of-concept engagements

  • Build trusted relationships with engineering leaders, architects, and developers, serving as their technical advisor

  • Translate customer requirements into solution designs, guiding them on best practices for rollout, prompt strategy, and context configuration

  • Develop and deliver technical presentations, whiteboard sessions, and hands-on workshops tailored to customer needs

  • Act as the customer’s technical advocate internally, influencing roadmap priorities and escalating feedback to Product and Engineering

  • Collaborate with post-sales teams to ensure a smooth handoff and successful customer onboarding

  • Maintain deep knowledge of Cursor’s capabilities and competitive landscape to position our value effectively

  • Support strategic account planning and help drive expansion opportunities with technical validation

You may be a fit if

  • You have strong communication skills and executive presence, equally comfortable coding alongside developers or presenting to CTOs.

  • You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle, modern engineering org structures, and developer productivity challenges

  • You have hands-on technical ability, and while you don’t need to be a full-time engineer, but you should be fluent in technical workflows, AI tooling, and debugging complex environments

  • You are customer-obsessed with a knack for translating technical details into business impact

  • You have experience in Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Pre-Sales, or Consulting for enterprise software

  • You thrive in a startup environment: resourceful, adaptable, and proactive in creating solutions

jobs.title: Deal Desk Manager, APJ
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

We're building out our Deal Desk function in APJ and looking for a high-ownership Deal Desk Manager to be one of our first people on the ground in the region. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role, sitting at the intersection of Sales, Legal, Finance, and Revenue Operations, partnering with our APJ sales team to structure, price, and close enterprise deals, and giving the region the fast, in-time-zone deal support it needs as it scales.

About the role

You'll be one of the first Deal Desk hires in APJ, working closely with the global Deal Desk team while becoming the go-to deal partner for reps across the region. The function is established globally and humming with volume — your job is to bring that same discipline to APJ and own deal support end-to-end for the region.

This person will own APJ deal desk as their domain and carry real strategic weight. Day-to-day, you'll be in the trenches on live deals — working through pricing and deal structure, building quotes and order forms, and shepherding deals through approvals to close. You'll also zoom out: spotting recurring friction in how APJ deals get done, and standing up the processes, playbooks, and guardrails that let the region scale.

What you'll do

  • Own day-to-day deal desk support for the APJ sales team — pricing, deal structure, quoting, and approvals — in-region and in-time-zone

  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to reps on deal strategy: pricing guidance, competitive positioning, negotiation approach, and contract structure

  • Build and manage quotes and order forms in Salesforce CPQ / Ironclad, and keep deals moving cleanly through the approval and closing process

  • Coordinate cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, and Billing to get non-standard terms reviewed and closed without slowing deals down

  • Stand up and scale APJ deal desk processes — turning recurring rep questions and one-off asks into repeatable playbooks, approval paths, and enablement

  • Apply and help evolve our consumption-based pricing model, surfacing patterns from APJ deal flow back to the global team

You may be a fit if

  • You have ~4–8+ years of experience across deal desk, deal/revenue operations, commercial strategy, consulting, investing, or sales strategy — and you've owned outcomes, not just tasks

  • You've worked on enterprise B2B deals, ideally in SaaS or infrastructure, with hands-on exposure to pricing, negotiation, and contract structure

  • You've operated in a high-volume deal environment and have a track record of systematizing how you work — playbooks, processes, approval frameworks

  • You're highly analytical — comfortable sizing deals, modeling pricing scenarios and ROI in Excel, and grounding recommendations in data

  • You have a point of view and the ownership to drive it — you don't wait to be told what to think, and you operate with urgency and little hand-holding

  • You collaborate well across Sales, Finance, and Legal, and can hold the line on pricing and process without becoming a bottleneck

  • You're excited to help build a function in-region rather than inherit a finished one

  • You're based in Singapore and able to support the APJ region

  • Bonus: experience with consumption-based or usage-based pricing, or standing up a deal desk function in a fast-scaling environment
