You'll be one of the first Deal Desk hires in APJ, working closely with the global Deal Desk team while becoming the go-to deal partner for reps across the region. The function is established globally and humming with volume — your job is to bring that same discipline to APJ and own deal support end-to-end for the region.

This person will own APJ deal desk as their domain and carry real strategic weight. Day-to-day, you'll be in the trenches on live deals — working through pricing and deal structure, building quotes and order forms, and shepherding deals through approvals to close. You'll also zoom out: spotting recurring friction in how APJ deals get done, and standing up the processes, playbooks, and guardrails that let the region scale.

What you'll do

 - Own day-to-day deal desk support for the APJ sales team — pricing, deal structure, quoting, and approvals — in-region and in-time-zone

 - Serve as a strategic thought partner to reps on deal strategy: pricing guidance, competitive positioning, negotiation approach, and contract structure

 - Build and manage quotes and order forms in Salesforce CPQ / Ironclad, and keep deals moving cleanly through the approval and closing process

 - Coordinate cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, and Billing to get non-standard terms reviewed and closed without slowing deals down

 - Stand up and scale APJ deal desk processes — turning recurring rep questions and one-off asks into repeatable playbooks, approval paths, and enablement

 - Apply and help evolve our consumption-based pricing model, surfacing patterns from APJ deal flow back to the global team

You may be a fit if

 - You have ~4–8+ years of experience across deal desk, deal/revenue operations, commercial strategy, consulting, investing, or sales strategy — and you've owned outcomes, not just tasks

 - You've worked on enterprise B2B deals, ideally in SaaS or infrastructure, with hands-on exposure to pricing, negotiation, and contract structure

 - You've operated in a high-volume deal environment and have a track record of systematizing how you work — playbooks, processes, approval frameworks

 - You're highly analytical — comfortable sizing deals, modeling pricing scenarios and ROI in Excel, and grounding recommendations in data

 - You have a point of view and the ownership to drive it — you don't wait to be told what to think, and you operate with urgency and little hand-holding

 - You collaborate well across Sales, Finance, and Legal, and can hold the line on pricing and process without becoming a bottleneck

 - You're excited to help build a function in-region rather than inherit a finished one

 - You're based in Singapore and able to support the APJ region

 - Bonus: experience with consumption-based or usage-based pricing, or standing up a deal desk function in a fast-scaling environment

jobs.title: Marketing Manager, Startup Events & Programs
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

As our Marketing Manager, Startup Events and Community, you'll be the growth engine behind Cursor for Startups, responsible for turning our startup strategy into high-impact programs that win the right early-stage companies, help founders get deeper value from Cursor, and turn our strongest founder-users into advocates.

This is a builder role for someone who's energized by the founder and startup community. We're building a focused program across top Seed–Series B startups, reaching them directly and through VC and accelerator ecosystems. You'll design the strategy for the events, community moments, and hackathons that create genuine advocacy and deeper product usage and make decisions about where we should show up and where we shouldn’t. If you want to be in and create the rooms with founders building the future, this is the role for you.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and requires working in-office.

What You'll Do

Program Architecture & Segment Ownership

  • Design the startup events playbook: Build and execute a data-driven marketing plan for the startup segment, focused on landing and growing usage within top Seed–Series B companies across YC and the broader ecosystem.

  • Own the founder funnel and footprint: Deploy a mix of founder events, hackathons, executive/founder roundtables, and community activations to acquire the right startups and drive them toward meaningful success using Cursor.

  • Build ecosystem relationships: Partner with VCs, accelerators, and other startup partners to reach their portfolio founders through growth programs, content, and co-hosted moments. Help identify which partners are worth going deep with.

  • Creativity: Fearlessly break the standard playbook by avoiding generic engagement formats - find out how founders actually build and gather and design around that.

  • Founder advocacy: Surface and amplify founder/customer stories worth telling, and feature them in our events. Become a trusted partner and peer to the founders using Cursor.

Measurement & Operational Excellence

  • Event orchestration: Own programs end to end, from ideation and promotion toonsite experience and follow-up. Keep it scrappy and high-signal; obsess over the details that make founders feel Cursor cares about them early.

  • Data-driven iteration: Track spend against real outcomes (activation, usage, retention, advocacy), not vanity metrics. Manage your budget toward the highest-impact investments and deprioritize what isn't working.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • GTM partnership: Work closely with the Events, Growth, PMM, and Field Engineering teams. Bring FEs into events to help founders build real automations, align on which startups show strong usage signals, and flag when a company is genuinely ready for an Enterprise conversation.

  • Product and marketing partnership: Be the "eyes and ears" of the founder community. Feed real-time insights on messaging resonance, credits/billing confusion, feature awareness, and competitive shifts back to Product and Marketing.

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience in or with startups: You have 4–7+ years in field, community, event, growth, or revenue marketing, ideally in B2B SaaS or developer tools. You understand founders and early-stage engineering teams, and how they buy, build, and talk to each other.

  • Builder mindset: You're a self-starter who can build a program from scratch and then obsessively optimize it based on data.

  • Community obsession: You genuinely like being around founders and builders, and you know the difference between a program that feels authentic to that community and one that feels like a vendor hard sell.

  • Storytelling: Your communication is sharp, credible, and founder-native. You can hold your own in a room full of technical founders.

Role Specifics

  • Field presence: Ability to travel (~20%) to host events, support hackathons, and connect with founders in-region.

  • Event craft: Experience producing standout events, from intimate founder dinners to high-energy hackathons, that people actually want to attend.

  • Location: In-office role based out of our San Francisco office.

jobs.title: Regional Vice President, Business Development APJ
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

Cursor's Business Development team drives our alternative routes to market: executive briefings, investor-convened roadshows, and zero-to-one market entry. This motion has opened enterprise markets across continents, converting executive access into qualified pipeline at a measured, proven rate.

We're looking for a Regional Vice President of Business Development to accelerate this motion in your region, working closely with our go-to-market leaders, customers, and partners to turn executive relationships into sourced pipeline for the account and partnership teams who carry those relationships forward.

What You'll Do:

  • Own our executive briefing network in-region. Build and maintain relationships across our largest customers and prospects.

  • Plan and lead executive engagement. Organize and facilitate meetings and multi-day trips for Cursor's executives in-region, directly owning the relationship until an account owner is assigned.

  • Drive new market entry and intelligence. Identify sub-regions, industries, and strategies for net-new customer acquisition, and help establish our presence in them.

  • Execute our regional enterprise growth strategy. Manage relationships across the full partner and customer lifecycle — from planning trips and roadshows to supporting account executives through close.

  • Forge new relationships. Build connections with partners, customers, and stakeholders in the region that contribute to our growth.

You May Be a Fit If You:

  • 12+ years of experience in business development, venture capital, or sales

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity, with a track record of hitting goals without a playbook

  • Have worked directly with customers and cross-functionally to get things done

  • Self-starter with clear evidence of professional initiative

  • Exceptional communicator with strong executive presence

  • Take pride in being a "super IC,” someone who does exceptional individual work

  • Familiar with the developer tooling ecosystem and current trends in AI

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers embed directly with customer engineering teams to ship production-grade Cursor workflows that measurably improve how they build software.

You’ll figure out what’s actually slowing a team down, design a practical solution, and own it end-to-end, from first discovery call through launch, iteration, and post-production support. This is not a demo role. You are responsible for systems that work in the real world.

What you’ll do

  • Lead discovery with customer engineers to identify the real bottleneck and define clear success metrics

  • Design and build Cursor-powered workflows (e.g., large-scale refactors, migrations, PR review loops, incident → fix pipelines, spec → implementation systems)

  • Ship a fast first version in days, then harden it into something reliable over weeks with proper rollout plans, monitoring, and iteration based on real usage

  • Own production quality: tracing, evals, metrics, debugging model behavior, latency/cost tradeoffs, and failure modes

  • Work directly with Staff+/Platform/Eng leaders — going deep in code while also communicating clearly about tradeoffs and results

  • Turn what you build into reusable patterns and push improvements back into the core Cursor product

You may be a fit if

  • You thrive in ambiguity and can turn fuzzy problems into clear scopes and shipped systems

  • You’ve built and owned AI-native workflows in production, not just prototypes, and have debugged real-world model failures

  • You’re comfortable leading discovery conversations and being accountable for customer outcomes

  • You build end-to-end - if it needs frontend, backend, infra, or prompt iteration, you’ll own it

  • You’ve handled production reliability before (metrics, alerts, safe rollouts, incident response)

  • You’re strong in Python and TypeScript/JavaScript and can ramp quickly on new stacks

jobs.title: Integrated Campaigns, AMER
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor is hiring a Senior Campaigns Manager to join our integrated campaigns team and help shape how Cursor shows up to enterprise audiences. This is a full-time, in-office role based at our San Francisco headquarters.

You will own high-priority campaigns that turn broad company priorities into focused, executable programs, working seamlessly across product marketing, sales, customer marketing, field, and leadership. The campaign strategies and programs you develop will shape our narrative in the market, create demand, generate & accelerate pipeline, and support customer growth.

This is a high-agency role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally comfortable identifying the right audience, building the campaign brief, shaping the message, coordinating cross-functional partners, launching programs across channels, and measuring what is actually working. Equal parts creative and analytical, you will think outside the box to propose original ideas and inventive audience engagement strategies, while bringing a data-driven mindset and the operational rigor required for high-impact execution.

What you’ll do

  • Concept, develop, and run integrated campaigns end to end.

    • Lead the strategy and audience selection through launch, optimization, and reporting.

    • Design the end-to-end campaign architecture, including the full-funnel content engine, channel strategies, promotional offers, program mix, and hand-offs from marketing to sales.

    • Translate company priorities into focused campaign plans with clear goals, messaging, milestones, owners, and success metrics.

    • Identify the highest-leverage assets needed to support campaign performance, including messaging frameworks, email nurtures, landing page copy, field activation ideas, customer story packaging, and sales-facing materials.

    • Bring multi-channel expertise to deliver campaigns via digital, web, email, online events, direct mail, social, events, sales plays, and more, all in partnership with functional and regional teams.

  • Strengthen cross-functional alignment, unifying all parts of the business around top go-to-market priorities.

    • Develop trusted relationships and facilitate integrated collaboration across product marketing, field marketing, performance marketing, growth marketing, strategic events, and design.

    • Work with creative partners to brief campaigns clearly and carry the message through across formats, channels, and moments in market.

    • Align closely with sales stakeholders to identify top priorities, build programs for strategic accounts, and ensure campaign initiatives are closely tied to revenue impact.

  • Establish measurement frameworks, KPIs, and scaleable processes.

    • Own campaign performance by measuring, analyzing, and reporting on the impact of campaign on pipeline, revenue, target account penetration, and the demand funnel. Share learnings regularly to improve overall campaign efficacy.

    • Work closely with operations and analytics partners to define the right KPIs, shape useful dashboards and reporting, and surface actionable account or campaign insights to the business.

    • Help establish repeatable campaign systems, workflows, and handoffs that let the function scale without becoming fragmented

  • Adapt campaigns for Cursor’s most strategic accounts and business priorities.

    • Build campaigns for enterprise and strategic audiences, including vertical, segment, buying-group, or use-case-specific motions. Translate vertical-specific messaging and proof points into campaign activations that make Cursor feel relevant to the priorities of different enterprise audiences.

    • Build 1:few ABM motions & ABM-at-scale programs for priority accounts or segments, in partnership with sales and field teams.

You may be a fit if

  • You’ve built integrated B2B campaigns across multiple channels and know how to connect content, email, digital, field, and sales motions into cohesive, high-impact motions.

  • You know how to turn a campaign idea into a real operating plan — from narrative and audience strategy through asset development, launch, field enablement, lead follow-up, and reporting.

  • You can take complex, ambiguous problems and bring structure, clarity, and a clear recommendation.

  • You’re comfortable being both strategic and hands-on — you can set direction, write a brief, shape the content, and help get the work shipped.

  • You have strong instincts for what makes a campaign cohesive across content, creative, distribution, and follow-up.

  • You’re comfortable working across both global strategy and regional execution, and can adapt campaigns thoughtfully for different markets without losing the core narrative.

  • You have strong instincts for what makes enterprise campaigns resonate with senior technical and business buyers.

  • You thrive in creative, fast-paced environments where original thinking and bias to action are celebrated.

  • You can shift between air cover demand generation and more targeted programs for strategic accounts, named accounts, and priority verticals.

  • You balance thoughtful dedication to quality with a clear focus on impact and ability to execute with sharp, decisive speed.

Experience that helps

  • You have 10+ years of experience owning integrated campaign strategy and execution for a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology company.

  • You have extensive familiarity with lead-routing & handoff. You’re able to diagnose funnel health and quickly course correct in tight alignment with your SDR counterparts.

  • You have a proven track record of building campaigns for enterprise audiences, including technical decision-makers, executives, and complex buying groups.

jobs.title: Product Education Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor ships fast. New models, new agentic capabilities, new workflows every week. The gap between what Cursor can do and what developers know how to build with it grows with every release. This role closes that gap, one lab, workshop, and tutorial at a time.

As a Product Education Engineer, you'll build the technical content and hands-on experiences that move developers from first install to deep, durable fluency. Code walkthroughs, labs, reference implementations, workshops, in-product learning, and whatever new formats we invent as we go. The demos and tutorials you ship should be things you built by pushing Cursor to its limits in your own work.

This is not a traditional customer education role. We're hiring engineers who teach, not curriculum developers who need external SMEs to write for them. You'll be the SME. You'll go deep on the product, deep with customers, and deep with the engineers building Cursor. You'll be the internal source of truth our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to when the product changes and they need to get up to speed.

You'll report to the Director of Product Education Engineering and partner with our Learning Experience Design team, who will help you translate technical depth into content that actually teaches.

What you’ll do

  • Build Cursor's technical learning library hands-on: code walkthroughs, tutorials, labs, workshops, reference implementations, and instructor-led training

  • Build high-quality demos, reference implementations, and workflow automations, using Cursor itself as part of your development process

  • Lead large-format workshops, technical deep dives, and hands-on enablement sessions that help engineering organizations adopt AI coding tools effectively and drive measurable outcomes

  • Be the technical translation layer between Product and the field. When Cursor ships new capabilities, our Field Engineers, ADMs, and Solutions Architects come to you to get up to speed

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, DevRel, and Go-to-Market ahead of major launches so new capabilities ship with clear educational framing, practical examples, and adoption paths on day one

  • Contribute technical guides, patterns, and best practices to Cursor's public technical content to help the broader developer community accelerate their work with Cursor

  • Design learning experiences for both developers and non-technical users (e.g. eng leaders evaluating rollout, PMs pairing with agents). Enterprise adoption depends on both, and our content has to meet each audience on its own terms

  • Experiment with new formats for education, including in-product learning, hands-on labs, interactive experiences, live teaching, and AI-native tutorials (e.g. guided flows that adapt to repo context and skill level)

  • Bring field signal back to Product and Engineering on where developers get stuck and what would unlock the next stage of adoption

  • Measure what works, tracking adoption and fluency gains rather than completion rates

You may be a fit if

  • You have 5+ years of experience in Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Consulting, technical enablement, or software engineering at a developer tools or platform company

  • You have a deep understanding of the software development lifecycle, modern engineering org structures, and how AI coding tools are reshaping how software gets built

  • You are an active power user of AI coding tools and have deeply customized your own developer workflow.

  • You have a point of view on what makes engineers more productive

  • You enjoy building scrappy, high-signal demos, integrations, and prototypes that clearly articulate what Cursor can enable, often using Cursor to accelerate your own development process

  • You have delivered large, high-impact workshops or technical training to engineering teams and know how to craft sessions that are engaging, hands-on, and outcomes-driven.

  • You have built the enablement infrastructure behind the workshops, including demo environments, content-freshness automation, and self-service tooling

  • You communicate complex technical concepts in clear, persuasive written and verbal form, especially when helping customers make strategic decisions about where and how to apply AI

  • You are excited by ambiguous, rapidly evolving problem spaces and enjoy iterating toward novel solutions hand-in-hand with customers

  • You care about customer success and operational excellence as much as you care about technical ingenuity

  • You have a builder mindset, high agency, and a bias toward experimenting with new educational formats rather than defaulting to traditional documentation

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Strategist
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Strategist to own our most strategic customer engagements - from first workshop through delivery. You'll sit with executive sponsors, surface the highest-value use cases, turn them into tightly scoped projects, then stay accountable for the outcome, working with the FDE.

You'll typically work in a pod of one Strategist and 1-2 FDEs. You own the executive relationship and the shape of delivery; the FDE embeds with the customer's team and owns the deeper production builds. You'll stay hands-on at the configuration layer week to week, including workflows, integrations, and platform tooling, partnering with the FDE where the build is most complex. You will translate technical build into business outcomes and own the adoption of the build.

This is for someone who combines technical credibility in agentic coding and LLMs with the executive presence to earn trust in the boardroom, and the judgment to keep engagements scoped tight, delivered fast, and worth repeating.

What you’ll do

  • Scope

    • Partner with customer executive sponsors to scope FDE projects — translating ambiguous business problems into concrete, time-boxed deliverables with clear ROI

    • Lead technical discovery and architecture reviews, surfacing integration complexity and infrastructure constraints to validate that every engagement is technically feasible

    Deliver

    • Work side by side with the FDE on the technical build — you own the configuration layer including workflows, settings, integrations, and platform tooling that don't require heavy custom code while the FDE owns the deeper production builds

    • Own technical enablement and adoption: run hands-on training, build playbooks and reference workflows, and coach the customer's team until they're self-sufficient. Adoption is measured by what their users do without you in the room

    • Monitor technical feasibility throughout delivery, adjusting scope with the sponsor when constraints emerge rather than letting engagements drift

    • Identify and scope expansion opportunities as they surface during delivery, in partnership with the account team

    • Escalate product gaps, integration friction, and recurring customer pain back to Product and Engineering with enough specificity to drive roadmap decisions

    • Build reusable playbooks that make the broader FDE org more capable over time

    Own the executive relationship

    • Establish and maintain the executive relationship on your engagements, serving as the primary point of contact from kickoff through handoff

    • Sell the vision and the plan to C-suite stakeholders who need to believe in both the outcome and the team delivering it

    • Translate between business outcomes and technical implementation in both directions — for the sponsor and for the build team

You may be a fit if

  • You've spent 6+ years in Solutions Architecture, Deployment Strategy, technical consulting, or an Engagement Manager seat where you owned scoping and delivery with a technical team in AI-production workflows

  • You understand agentic coding and LLMs well enough to hold your own with senior eng: how they behave in production, where they fail, and what a resilient workflow looks like (you don't need to be the person writing the production code)

  • You're comfortable hands-on with Cursor workflows, integrations, and platform config, and can read enough Python / JS-TS to partner with an FDE

  • You've shipped AI-native workflows past the prototype stage and can tell a real production constraint from a nice-to-have

  • You can walk into an unfamiliar enterprise eng org, find the highest-leverage intervention fast, and scope something that delivers concrete value in weeks, not quarters

  • You have the executive presence to own the C-suite relationship and the technical credibility to earn trust with their eng leads

  • Domain depth in FSI, insurance, telecom, high-tech, healthcare/life sciences, or semiconductor is a strong plus

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships & Growth Lead — Civilian Government
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the Role

Cursor is the AI code editor used by software engineers across the federal government and the contractors who support them. We are now building a dedicated motion into the civilian Cabinet-level agency ecosystem — DHS, DOJ, DOE, Treasury, HHS, State, and the dozens of bureaus and offices within them that run significant software development operations.

This role owns Cursor's civilian government channel: building relationships with the prime contractors, systems integrators, and federal consulting firms that develop and operate software for Cabinet-level civilian agencies. The mission is to embed Cursor into the software development workflows of every engineer building for the federal civilian government.

Civilian agencies run some of the most complex software in the world — border management at CBP, financial systems at Treasury, scientific computing at DOE national labs, law enforcement infrastructure at FBI. The developers inside those programs need better tools, and Cursor is already being used by individuals inside these agencies. This role builds the formal channel motion to make it the standard.

This is a senior individual contributor role with revenue ownership, reporting directly to sales leadership.

What You'll Do

Prime contractor and channel partnerships

  • Own and grow Cursor's relationships with prime contractors and systems integrators focused on civilian agency programs: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte Government and Public Services (GPS), Booz Allen Hamilton (Civil division), Leidos Civil, SAIC, CACI, Maximus Federal, Guidehouse, ICF, and contractors supporting MITRE-operated FFRDC programs

  • Negotiate and close partnership agreements — reseller arrangements, teaming agreements, and approved vendor designations — that embed Cursor into software delivery workflows on civilian agency programs

  • Work with prime BD and program management teams to co-sell Cursor into new civilian agency contract awards at the proposal stage

  • Identify and develop relationships with federal consulting firms and boutique civilian-agency integrators that can serve as channel partners or pull-through vehicles

Agency end-user pull-through

  • Build relationships inside DHS (CBP, USCIS, ICE, TSA, CISA, FEMA, Coast Guard), DOJ (FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS), DOE (NNSA, national laboratory network including Sandia, Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore, PNNL, Argonne, Oak Ridge), and other Cabinet-level agencies at the IT, software engineering, and digital transformation leadership level

  • Engage agency CIOs, CDOs, and digital service offices to build awareness and preference for Cursor within civilian agency software development standards and procurement pipelines

  • Develop relationships with the US Digital Service (USDS), GSA (18F, Login.gov, cloud.gov), and agency-embedded digital transformation teams that influence tooling standards across the civilian government

  • Represent Cursor at ACT-IAC events, AFCEA Federal, agency industry days, and civilian government technology conferences; establish Cursor's presence in the federal civilian IT community

Revenue and pipeline

  • Own a revenue target for civilian government channel business

  • Build and manage a pipeline of prime contractor partnerships and program-level co-sell opportunities across civilian agency programs

  • Forecast and report on channel pipeline with the same rigor as direct enterprise deals

  • Identify and pursue contract vehicles relevant to civilian software tools: GSA IT Schedule 70, CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3, and agency-specific BPAs and IDIQs

Cross-functional

  • Work with Cursor's legal and compliance teams on teaming agreements, vendor qualification, and FedRAMP authorization planning — civilian agencies are more likely to require FedRAMP than DoD, and this candidate should be able to navigate those conversations honestly and strategically

  • Partner with Field Engineering on technical evaluations and POCs inside prime contractor and agency developer environments

  • Channel civilian agency developer feedback and product requirements back to Cursor's roadmap team — DOE national labs in particular will push requirements for high-performance computing, scientific workflows, and air-gapped environments that no other customer segment will surface

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Active Secret clearance — non-negotiable; candidates without an active Secret clearance will not be considered

  • US Citizenship required

  • 5+ years of channel sales, BD, or partnership management experience inside the federal civilian government market, with direct exposure to Cabinet-level agency programs

  • Existing relationships at one or more prime contractors or systems integrators active in the civilian agency market at the BD, program management, or technical leadership level

  • Understanding of civilian government procurement mechanics: GSA Schedule 70, IDIQ vehicles (CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3), agency-specific BPAs, and the role of FedRAMP in civilian agency software procurement

  • Track record of standing up or expanding channel/partner relationships that drove material software or technology revenue ($500K+) in the civilian federal market

  • Comfortable navigating both the prime-facing channel layer (BD, program managers, contracting) and the end-user pull-through layer (agency software engineers, IT leads, digital transformation offices)

Strong plus

  • Active TS/SCI or DOE Q clearance

  • Prior experience or service at a Cabinet-level civilian agency in a software, IT, data, or digital transformation role

  • Experience selling developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or SDLC tooling through or alongside civilian federal prime contractors

  • Existing relationships at DHS (any component), DOJ (FBI, DEA, or USMS), DOE (NNSA or national laboratory), or Treasury/HHS digital service offices

  • Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization processes and the ability to position a pre-authorization vendor's roadmap credibly in front of civilian agency procurement teams

  • Network within the civilian federal prime ecosystem: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte GPS, Booz Allen Civil, Leidos Civil, SAIC Civil

  • Understanding of DOE national laboratory culture and procurement — national labs operate outside standard civilian agency procurement in meaningful ways and represent some of the largest software development communities in the federal government

Why this role

Cabinet-level civilian agencies employ tens of thousands of software developers and spend billions on technology contracts annually. Cursor is already being used by engineers inside these agencies and the contractors that support them. The formal channel motion does not yet exist. This role builds it from scratch, with a product developers choose independently, a growing prime contractor presence to build on, and direct access to Cursor's GTM and product leadership.

 - Work with Cursor's legal and compliance teams on teaming agreements, vendor qualification, and FedRAMP authorization planning — civilian agencies are more likely to require FedRAMP than DoD, and this candidate should be able to navigate those conversations honestly and strategically

 - Partner with Field Engineering on technical evaluations and POCs inside prime contractor and agency developer environments

 - Channel civilian agency developer feedback and product requirements back to Cursor's roadmap team — DOE national labs in particular will push requirements for high-performance computing, scientific workflows, and air-gapped environments that no other customer segment will surface
   

What We're Looking For

Required

 - Active Secret clearance — non-negotiable; candidates without an active Secret clearance will not be considered

 - US Citizenship required

 - 5+ years of channel sales, BD, or partnership management experience inside the federal civilian government market, with direct exposure to Cabinet-level agency programs

 - Existing relationships at one or more prime contractors or systems integrators active in the civilian agency market at the BD, program management, or technical leadership level

 - Understanding of civilian government procurement mechanics: GSA Schedule 70, IDIQ vehicles (CIO-SP4, Alliant 2/3), agency-specific BPAs, and the role of FedRAMP in civilian agency software procurement

 - Track record of standing up or expanding channel/partner relationships that drove material software or technology revenue ($500K+) in the civilian federal market

 - Comfortable navigating both the prime-facing channel layer (BD, program managers, contracting) and the end-user pull-through layer (agency software engineers, IT leads, digital transformation offices)

Strong plus

 - Active TS/SCI or DOE Q clearance

 - Prior experience or service at a Cabinet-level civilian agency in a software, IT, data, or digital transformation role

 - Experience selling developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or SDLC tooling through or alongside civilian federal prime contractors

 - Existing relationships at DHS (any component), DOJ (FBI, DEA, or USMS), DOE (NNSA or national laboratory), or Treasury/HHS digital service offices

 - Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization processes and the ability to position a pre-authorization vendor's roadmap credibly in front of civilian agency procurement teams

 - Network within the civilian federal prime ecosystem: Accenture Federal Services, Deloitte GPS, Booz Allen Civil, Leidos Civil, SAIC Civil

 - Understanding of DOE national laboratory culture and procurement — national labs operate outside standard civilian agency procurement in meaningful ways and represent some of the largest software development communities in the federal government

Why this role

Cabinet-level civilian agencies employ tens of thousands of software developers and spend billions on technology contracts annually. Cursor is already being used by engineers inside these agencies and the contractors that support them. The formal channel motion does not yet exist. This role builds it from scratch, with a product developers choose independently, a growing prime contractor presence to build on, and direct access to Cursor's GTM and product leadership.

jobs.title: Revenue Accounting
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor is rethinking how software gets built. We want the same ambition for how revenue is accounted for: one accountable owner from contract and billing reality → books → controls → reporting → audit, with processes that stay fast as the business changes. You will own that thread, build best-in-class close and controllership deliverables, and use Cursor itself to automate repetitive work, tighten documentation, and move faster with fewer errors—not as a gimmick, but as how a modern revenue team should operate.

You should be comfortable going from first principles, making decisions with incomplete information, and building processes that don’t yet exist.

We’re in-person in San Francisco (North Beach) and New York (Manhattan).

What you’ll do

  • Run and improve the monthly/quarterly close for revenue, deferred revenue, unbilled receivables, and related balance sheet accounts—reconciliations, JEs, and flux that hold up to scrutiny.

  • Run revenue-related reconciliations and journal entries; investigate and resolve discrepancies.

  • Perform flux analysis on revenue; explain drivers to leadership and partner teams in plain language.

  • Partner early on pricing, packaging, promotions, credits/refunds, and billing logic so revenue recognition and operational readiness are clear before changes ship.

  • Work with User Ops, Finance Systems, Finance Data, and Billing so that what the product and pipes produce is what the GL reflects—especially for high-volume and automated revenue streams.

  • Help select, implement, and improve billing and revenue systems (e.g., NetSuite, Stripe, or similar)

  • Design, document, and maintain internal controls over revenue and order-to-cash; maintain audit-ready evidence (including control matrices and testing support).

How you’ll work — Cursor as a multiplier

We hire people who want to set the standard, not just check boxes. In this role, that includes using Cursor to:

  • Automate workstreams—scripts, reconciliation helpers, repeatable close steps, and lightweight tooling that reduce manual drag and human error.

  • Produce best-in-class deliverables—clear memos, control narratives, close packages, and analyses that are easy for leadership, audit, and partners to consume.

  • Create efficiencies—templates, checklists, and workflows that scale as headcount and transaction volume grow.

  • Move faster safely—pair AI-assisted drafting and exploration with your judgment on GAAP, controls, and what actually happened economically.

You may be a fit if

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance (or equivalent experience); CPA or equivalent strongly preferred.

  • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience with meaningful revenue accounting depth

  • Strong command of ASC 606

  • Experience with subscription and usage-based SaaS and high volume self-service revenue

  • Experience designing and implementing systems and integrations that keep accounting data flowing automatically from source to GL

  • SQL or other data skills for reconciliations of large datasets

  • Hands on experience with Netsuite, Stripe, HubiFi, Salesforce, or other similar tools

  • Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally, influence without authority, and deliver in a fast-changing, high-growth environment.

  • Excellent attention to detail, communication, and ownership—you spot issues, propose fixes, and drive them to completion.

jobs.title: Manager, Channel & Partners
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Cursor is building its partner ecosystem across APJ, and this is a build-from-the-ground-up role at the centre of it. As the in-market partner builder for your market, you own the partner business end to end. You set the strategy, stand it up, and run it, all at the same time. You work as the business partner to the in-market Regional Vice President, turning their go-to-market priorities into partner-led pipeline and co-sell wins. Two engines drive the market, Technology partnerships and Transformation partnerships, both building on relationships Cursor already holds.

Japan is a partner-first market. You cannot operate effectively without strong local partners, and this is the most pressing of our APJ in-market needs despite being at the earliest stage. This is a standing start: you will land Cursor's first local partners in Japan, open co-sell motions, and stand up FDE capacity in a market with no coverage today.

This is a team of one in-market with a speed mandate. You report into the Director of Partnerships APJ, which keeps the craft and standards under partnerships without splitting your accountability to the market.

This is an in-market role. You will spend a significant share of your time in person with partner principals, delivery teams, and customers across your market, and you will work closely with a small, high-talent-density global partnerships team that values in-person collaboration and fast, direct communication.

What you'll do

• Own the in-market partner business from concept to completion. Set the market partner strategy and sequencing from greenfield, then execute it personally.

• Accelerate Cursor's global partners into your market and incubate them to productivity, across Technology and Transformation partnerships.

• Where gaps exist, recruit, onboard, and manage local partners from the ground up.

• Build and run co-sell motions, stand up FDE (forward deployed engineer) capacity, and drive C-level access and value-amplification programs through to landed wins.

• Turn partner relationships into qualified pipeline and closed co-sell revenue that feeds the in-market RVP number.

• Build the data picture for your market and use it to drive decisions, priorities, and forecasting.

• Own the operating system that keeps it repeatable: reporting, tracking, tiering, onboarding flows, partner QBRs, and cadence.

• Act as business partner to the in-market RVP, translating their go-to-market priorities into partner motion and giving them a clear, data-backed view of the business.

• Take ambiguous problems, from routes to market and contracting to partner economics, co-sell mechanics, channel conflict, localisation, FDE accreditation, and customer access, and drive them to a working outcome without the path laid out for you.

You may be a fit if

• You are fluent in Japanese and deeply understand the local technology and services partner ecosystem, especially SIs/GSIs. In a partner-first market, this is essential.

• You have professional working proficiency in English. You will engage consistently with HQ and present plans to English-speaking stakeholders, so you can operate and communicate confidently in English. Fluency in both Japanese and English is the highest-value combination for this role.

• You are a builder-operator, a doer rather than a coordinator, energized by owning a business from greenfield and running it as it grows.

• You have built and scaled technology, consulting, GSI, ideally in enterprise software, and carried a number against that work.

• You are fluent across partner business plans, program mechanics, enablement, and co-sell economics, and comfortable being accountable for the outcomes.

• You make decisions from data and can stand up the reporting and operating cadence yourself.

• You build durable relationships with partner principals and alliance leads, the kind of person partners choose to invest behind.

• You navigate negotiation and channel conflict with judgment, and you identify and influence the right internal and external people quickly.

• You operate credibly across diverse markets and decision-making styles, and you move fast.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Pretraining
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We’re looking for Software Engineers to build the data systems behind our frontier coding models’ initial training. You’ll work on large-scale crawling, data platform, and pipeline infrastructure, turning raw dumps into the datasets our models train on, and making iteration with researchers fast and reliable.

  • The Data Quality team owns the entire road between raw internet-scale data and the tokens that train frontier models. This team makes sure the right data, in the right form, hits the training clusters on time and at the quality bar required to push the scaling curve. This is done by building our own models, our own high-performance pipelines, and by running the experiments that prove the data is actually stellar.

  • The Data Platform Team owns the infrastructure and pipelines that transform raw data dumps into training-ready datasets. This team improves the speed, reliability, and developer experience of our initial training data pipelines so researchers can quickly experiment with new data sources, quality filters, taxonomies, multimodal data, and data mixes that improve model performance.

  • The Crawling team owns large-scale web crawling and parsing that feeds the top of the funnel for initial training. They discover, schedule, fetch, and parse public web content so high-quality documents become the raw scrapes that Data Quality and Data Platform turn into tokens and mixes. This is deep distributed systems work with real ownership: host coverage and prioritization, fetch success under antibot and trap content, HTML/document parsing quality, and reliability of the crawl infrastructure that must continuously supply every downstream data pipeline.

What you’ll do

  • on the Data Quality Team:

    • Build and own high-throughput, fully telemetered data pipelines that process frontier-scale data with end-to-end traceability. If something breaks or drifts, your systems will tell us before the training run does.

    • Train and ship models that classify, rank, filter, clean, and identify data at extreme throughput. These models have to be both accurate and fast enough to sit in the critical path without becoming the bottleneck.

    • Design and run scaling-ladder experiments on data-mixture, repeatability, and quality depth that turn “this dataset feels good” into hard evidence the training team can trust.

    • Partner tightly with Data Acquisition to hunt down missing or low-quality sources, and with the training teams to close the loop on what actually moves loss and downstream evals.

    • Treat data quality as a systems problem and a research problem. You will write performance-critical code one week and design careful experiments the next.

  • on the Data Platform Team:

    • Build the platform that turns raw web, code, multimodal, and acquired data into training-ready datasets for frontier pretraining runs.

    • Own the pipelines, orchestration, and tooling that make pretraining data iteration fast, reliable, observable, and reproducible at scale.

    • Create clear signals for data quality, lineage, freshness, and pipeline health so researchers can trust what goes into each run.

    • Partner with initial training, crawling, data quality, and acquisition teams to turn new data ideas into measurable improvements in loss, evals, and model capability.

  • on the Crawling Team:

    • Build and scale the web crawling systems that discover, schedule, fetch, and parse high-quality documents across the open web for initial training.

    • Improve URL seeding, scoring, and fair host scheduling so crawl capacity lands on the hosts and pages that matter most for model quality.

    • Raise crawl success and parsing quality — defeating antibot failures, improving extractors, and capturing content we previously could not get cleanly.

    • Debug and harden complex crawl infrastructure end-to-end for availability, recovery, and ingestion lag, and automate delivery of crawl datasets into the data pipeline.

    • Work independently (and alongside AI agents) and partner with Data Quality and Data Platform so new coverage shows up as better tokens in training runs.

You may be a fit if

  • You have a strong infrastructure or data platform background, and ideally a spike of outlier depth somewhere (crawling/search infra is a plus, not a hard requirement)

  • You are a high-slope engineer who has moved unusually fast — for example, staff-level ownership within a few years — or you bring deep domain experience

  • You are able to architect and ship end-to-end with high ownership, debug complex systems independently, and work alongside AI agents

  • You have strong intuitions about large-scale distributed systems

  • You’re excited to learn how pre-training data shapes model quality, and want the ownership and visibility that comes with building systems that feed frontier training runs

#LI-DNI

jobs.title: Solutions Architect - India
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

We’re hiring Solution Architects to help the world’s best engineering organizations figure out what AI-native software development actually looks like in production.

This is a deeply technical, post-sale role embedded inside Cursor’s most strategic enterprise accounts. You’ll work directly with engineering teams to roll out high-impact workflows, accelerate adoption, and help organizations fundamentally rethink how software gets built with AI.

Solution Architects sit at the center of long-term customer transformation. You’ll help customers move from initial excitement to deeply integrating engineering workflows that teams rely on every day. That means understanding how modern software organizations operate, identifying where Cursor can create the most leverage, and helping customers scale adoption across teams, platforms, and workflows over time.

This role is highly hands-on. You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

 

What you’ll do

Help Engineering Teams Adopt AI-Native Development

  • Roll out Cursor across strategic engineering organizations

  • Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

  • Help developers integrate Cursor into real production workflows, not isolated demos

  • Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

  • Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly

Expand Cursor Across the Organization

  • Identify where Cursor should expand next inside the customer environment

  • Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

  • Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

  • Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

  • Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments

Become a Trusted Technical Partner

  • Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

  • Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

  • Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

  • Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

  • Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves

Drive Real Customer Outcomes

  • Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

  • Connect Cursor usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

  • Help customers communicate the value of Cursor internally and build momentum for broader adoption

  • Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization

Help Make Cursor Indispensable

  • Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

  • Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Cursor over time

  • Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

  • Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without

Shape the Future of the Product

  • Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

  • Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

  • Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

  • Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

 

You may be a fit if

  • You have a strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

  • You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

  • You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

  • You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

  • You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

  • You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

  • You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

  • You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

  • You are willing to travel to customers needed

You’ll configure environments, design workflows, run enablement sessions, and solve technical problems directly with developers and platform teams inside complex enterprise environments. You’ll also help engineering leaders think through rollout strategy, workflow evolution, and the long-term architecture for AI-native development.

The best Solution Architects combine deep technical credibility with strong product instincts, high ownership, and the ability to influence how large engineering organizations evolve. Solution Architects are also equally comfortable debugging CI workflows, leading architecture reviews, and helping executives understand where AI changes the economics of software development.

HELP ENGINEERING TEAMS ADOPT AI-NATIVE DEVELOPMENT

 - Roll out Cursor across strategic engineering organizations

 - Configure environments, design workflows, and run hands-on enablement sessions

 - Help developers integrate Cursor into real production workflows, not isolated demos

 - Drive fast time-to-value and durable adoption across teams

 - Identify workflow friction and solve problems quickly


EXPAND CURSOR ACROSS THE ORGANIZATION

 - Identify where Cursor should expand next inside the customer environment

 - Help engineering organizations evolve from isolated usage to company-wide adoption

 - Design rollout strategies for new workflows, teams, and platform groups

 - Partner with customers to operationalize AI-assisted development at scale

 - Work closely with Account Executives during major expansion moments


BECOME A TRUSTED TECHNICAL PARTNER

 - Build deep relationships with developers, platform teams, engineering leadership, and executive stakeholders

 - Lead architecture reviews, technical working sessions, and strategic planning discussions

 - Advise customers on developer productivity, workflow design, governance, and AI adoption strategy

 - Coordinate across Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to unblock customer progress

 - Help organizations navigate workflow and operational change as AI-native development evolves


DRIVE REAL CUSTOMER OUTCOMES

 - Help customers translate adoption into measurable engineering impact

 - Connect Cursor usage to outcomes like faster iteration cycles, improved developer productivity, workflow efficiency, and engineering quality

 - Help customers communicate the value of Cursor internally and build momentum for broader adoption

 - Turn successful deployments into repeatable workflow patterns across the organization


HELP MAKE CURSOR INDISPENSABLE

 - Deepen workflow adoption and long-term product stickiness

 - Monitor competitive risk and help customers standardize on Cursor over time

 - Support recovery plans when adoption slows or competing tools gain traction

 - Help customers build workflows they can’t imagine operating without


SHAPE THE FUTURE OF THE PRODUCT

 - Bring structured feedback from strategic customers into Product and Engineering

 - Identify emerging workflow patterns, friction points, and enterprise requirements

 - Help shape new capabilities through lighthouse customers and design partnerships

 - Turn successful customer workflows into reusable playbooks and reference patterns

 


YOU MAY BE A FIT IF

 - You have a strong technical background in software engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, or developer tooling

 - You have experience in customer-facing technical roles such as Solution Architect, Solutions Engineer, Forward Deployed Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Enterprise Architect, or similar

 - You have the ability to work hands-on with engineering teams while also operating strategically with technical leadership

 - You have a strong understanding of developer workflows, SDLC tooling, integrations, CI/CD systems, governance, and enterprise engineering environments

 - You have excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly across both technical and executive audiences

 - You have strong instincts around workflow design, adoption strategy, and driving workflow change across engineering teams

 - You have high ownership, strong execution skills, and comfort operating in fast-moving environments with ambiguity

 - You have a passion for developer tooling and strong conviction around how AI will reshape software engineering

 - You are willing to travel to customers needed

jobs.title: Software Engineer, RL Data
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

Software Engineer, Reinforcement learning

Cursor is building the future of coding. We train frontier coding agents and scale RL on real user data to make them increasingly effective.

About the role

As a Software Engineer on the RL Data team at Cursor, you'll create the tasks, rewards, and environments that train our coding agents. The team owns the data that goes into training: what the model is asked to do, how we score it, and the setups it learns in.

What you’ll do

  • Designing a task set that teaches a specific agent capability, then iterating on it from traces and evals until the model actually gets better.

  • Reading a pile of agent traces, finding a failure mode or a surprising behavior, and building a system that surfaces more of the same.

  • Turning a one-off recipe into something other teams can reuse: better rewards, cleaner environments, tighter data quality.

  • Partnering with research on whether a dataset is actually teaching the thing we think it is.

You may be a fit if

  • You write careful, fast code and have strong software engineering fundamentals.

  • You like setting tasks: breaking a fuzzy capability into something concrete you can measure.

  • You have an infra, data, or distributed systems background. RL experience is a plus, not a requirement.

  • You enjoy looking at messy real-world agent behavior and turning it into a dataset or a tool.

jobs.title: RVP, Geo Enterprise East
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

As RVP, Geo Enterprise Sales at Cursor, you'll build and lead the organization responsible for revenue growth across a major geographic enterprise segment. You'll hire and develop frontline sales leaders, set territory and account strategy at scale, and personally engage in the most strategic, executive-level relationships in the region. You'll partner with engineering leaders — from CTOs to VPs of Engineering — to show how Cursor transforms developer productivity, and drive a land-and-expand motion across sophisticated software companies.

This is a second-line leadership role: you'll scale through managers who lead high-performing Account Executives, while staying close enough to the business to shape strategy, unblock deals, and set the bar for excellence. It requires deep technical fluency, command of complex enterprise buying processes, and a genuine passion for AI-powered developer tools. You'll be a foundational leader in our enterprise sales organization.

What you’ll do

  • Build, hire, and lead a team of frontline sales leaders (and, through them, a high-performing Geo Enterprise AE organization); own forecasting, pipeline health, and quota attainment across the region.

  • Set and execute go-to-market strategy for a named geographic enterprise territory — driving new logo acquisition, expansion revenue, and long-term strategic growth.

  • Personally engage in the largest, most strategic deals — leading complex, multi-threaded sales cycles across Engineering, Product, Security, Procurement, Legal, and executive stakeholders.

  • Coach and develop sales leaders to build teams of trusted product experts who can guide prospects through trials, technical evaluations, security reviews, and large-scale rollouts.

  • Build executive relationships across strategic accounts and represent Cursor at the CTO / VP Engineering / C-level.

  • Establish clear ROI frameworks tied to developer productivity and AI adoption, and ensure your leaders and teams apply them consistently.

  • Serve as the voice of the enterprise customer to leadership, shaping roadmap, packaging, deployment, and GTM strategy.

  • Partner closely with Field Engineering and the AI Deployment team to ensure outcomes from proof of concept through production deployment and expansion.

  • Partner closely with Field Engineering and the AI Deployment team to ensure outcomes from proof of concept through production deployment and expansion.

  • Build repeatable playbooks for outbound hunting, enterprise deal execution, and land-and-expand so the region scales with quality, not just headcount.

  • Operate as a true builder: stand up or scale the region with a bias for hands-on involvement in account strategy, executive engagement, and enabling your leaders to win.

You may be a fit if

  • You have 12+ years of enterprise technology sales experience, including 5+ years leading and scaling quota-carrying sales organizations, with meaningful experience as a second-line leader (managing managers), ideally in developer tools, technical SaaS, infrastructure, or emerging technologies.

  • You have a consistent track record of building and leading teams (and leaders) that land new logos, expand strategic accounts, and exceed quota.

  • You're a builder — you've stood up or scaled a region or multi-team organization from the ground up, with a bias for hands-on involvement in outbound motion, account mapping, and executive deal strategy.

  • You're comfortable navigating complex enterprise sales cycles and coaching leaders and reps to sell to technical stakeholders — from senior ICs to CTOs and C-level executives.

  • You understand how sophisticated software companies buy developer tools, and can translate that into regional strategy, hiring plans, and enablement.

  • You bring an analytical approach to pipeline and forecasting, combined with the creative, tactical instincts to unblock deals and coach leaders through them.

  • You're an excellent communicator and leader who builds trust across all levels — your leaders, your broader team, customers, and Cursor executives alike.

  • You're passionate about AI and excited by the idea that transforming how software gets written is one of the most important problems to work on right now.

jobs.title: Sales Development Leader - APJ
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

We are hiring a Sales Development Leader, APJ to build and lead Cursor’s Sales Development organization across Asia Pacific. Based in our Singapore office, this is a frontline leadership role responsible for hiring, coaching, and developing a high-performing team of Account Associates that generate pipeline and accelerate customer adoption across the region.

This isn’t a traditional SDR organization focused solely on cold outreach. Our Sales Development team partners closely with Growth, Marketing, RevOps, and Sales to identify buying signals, engage customers at the right moment, and create highly personalized outreach informed by product usage, PLG signals, and creative automation. You’ll help your team balance modern, signal-based engagement with disciplined outbound prospecting to consistently create new opportunities across commercial and enterprise accounts.

You’ll be responsible for building a strong team culture, driving execution against pipeline goals, coaching early-career talent, and continuously improving how Cursor engages prospective customers across APJ. This role is ideal for a hands-on sales leader who enjoys coaching people, experimenting with new approaches, and building scalable operating rhythms in a fast-growing company.

 

This is a full-time, in-office leadership role based in our Singapore office.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Hire, onboard, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Account Associates supporting the APJ business.

  • Lead the team’s day-to-day execution against pipeline generation goals, activity metrics, and conversion targets.

  • Partner with Growth, RevOps, Marketing, and Sales to execute signal-based outbound programs leveraging product usage, PLG insights, events, and other buying signals.

  • Help define and refine regional sales development playbooks that combine modern automation with highly personalized customer engagement.

  • Coach Account Associates on prospecting, discovery, qualification, messaging, and customer engagement to consistently improve pipeline quality.

  • Establish a strong operating cadence through regular pipeline reviews, one-on-ones, performance coaching, team meetings, and career development.

  • Monitor team performance, identify trends, and use data to continuously improve productivity, conversion rates, and execution.

  • Collaborate closely with Commercial and Enterprise Sales leaders to ensure high-quality pipeline generation and seamless opportunity handoffs.

  • Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, accountability, and continuous learning.

  • Develop future sales talent by creating clear career pathways into Account Executive and other GTM roles across Cursor.

     

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of SaaS sales experience, including experience leading frontline Sales Development or SDR teams.

  • Proven success hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing SDRs or Account Associates in a fast-paced technology company.

  • Experience building predictable outbound pipeline generation through a combination of prospecting, automation, and data-driven experimentation.

  • Strong operational discipline with experience managing team performance through metrics, coaching, and structured operating cadences.

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with Marketing, Growth, RevOps, and Sales to improve pipeline generation and conversion.

  • Passion for coaching and developing early-career sales talent into successful GTM professionals.

  • Curiosity about AI, developer tools, or technical products, with the ability to help teams engage technical buyers effectively.

  • Comfortable operating in a high-growth, fast-changing environment where experimentation and continuous improvement are expected.

  • Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills with a collaborative, builder’s mindset.

  • Experience with AI products, growth automation platforms, PLG motions, or developer-focused technology is a plus.

jobs.title: Account Executive, Commercial Expansion - New York
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Our mission is to automate coding. The first step in our journey is to build the best tool for professional programmers, using a combination of inventive research, design, and engineering. Our organization is very flat, and our team is small and talent dense. We particularly like people who are truth-seeking, passionate, and creative. We enjoy spirited debate, crazy ideas, and shipping code.

About the role

Our Commercial team focuses on high-growth companies where AI adoption is moving fast and deals are often enterprise-sized.

We're hiring our first Commercial Expansion Account Executive to own a book of existing accounts, deliver meaningful value to customers, drive expansion, and ensure successful renewals. This is a proactive, sales-led role focused on unlocking the next wave of growth within some of Cursor's most exciting customers.

What You'll Do

  • Own a portfolio of existing commercial customers and be accountable for expansion, net revenue retention, and renewals, landing new business units, deepening adoption, and cross-selling Cursor's platform

  • Proactively multi-thread into engineering, data, and product leadership to identify opportunities, position additional capabilities (agent-first workflows, new features, frontier models), and turn initial lands into multi-year, multi-product relationships

  • Monitor usage commitments closely and reach out long before customers exhaust their pre-commit to revisit value delivered, explain Cursor's evolving product and model landscape, and right-size the next phase of usage and commercial structure

  • Run high-judgment renewal motions - from transactional, email-led renewals to complex, multi-stakeholder negotiations involving solutions, product, and leadership

  • Help shape and execute an emerging tiering strategy across your book (Tier 1 strategic accounts vs. transactional tail) and ruthlessly prioritize your time accordingly

  • Stay on top of the fast-changing AI ecosystem - new models, pricing shifts, product capabilities - and translate that into clear, value-led narratives for customers

  • Collaborate closely with Product, Support, RevOps, and Sales Leadership to tighten feedback loops from the field and level up how Cursor sells and supports commercial customers

What Success Looks Like

  • You deliver meaningful value to customers, helping them stay ahead of the curve by growing adoption and transforming the way they build software.

  • You consistently hit or exceed renewal and expansion targets across your book of business.

  • Your Tier 1 accounts see meaningful year-over-year growth in both usage and revenue, and you can point to specific multi-threaded plays you ran to make it happen.

  • Customers trust you as a strategic partner who can explain Cursor's roadmap and pricing, and how the broader AI landscape is shifting and what that means for them.

  • Internally, Sales and Product leaders rely on you for signal on what's working (and what isn't) in our expansion and renewal playbook.

You may be a fit if

  • You have 2+ years of closing experience in a high-velocity B2B SaaS environment

  • You have meaningful expansion and renewal experience: you've owned a book of business, run renewal cycles, and can walk through how you turned an initial land into significant

  • You have experience selling technical products, including dev tools, infrastructure, data/AI platforms, payments/fintech, or similarly complex, multi-stakeholder solutions

  • You have a strong commercial and strategic mindset: comfortable navigating change, usage-based models, and explaining "why things are changing" in a way that builds trust
